exposure: skin-to-skin contact with breastfeeding in the first hour of life
cohort: 959 mother-infant pairs who attended a specialized breastfeeding clinic in São Paulo, Brazil, between 2004 and 2010.
finding: While exclusive breastfeeding rates were higher in the group that practiced skin-to-skin contact with breastfeeding within the first hour of life, there was no association with the duration of exclusive breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Cesarean section and forceps deliveries were identified as risk factors for not practicing skin-to-skin contact with breastfeeding in the first hour of life.
